newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Erbakan sees end to Iraq force mandate.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Erbakan sees end to Iraq force mandate.

text.p: Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan on Friday predicted an end to the mandate of a Turkey-based Western air force that shields the Kurds of northern Iraq from any attack by Baghdad.
But Western diplomats say the U.S., British and French force would probably be replaced by a similar operation.
"It has come to the point where Provide Comfort's duties will be ended on December 31," Erbakan told reporters before a cabinet meeting.
The mandate of the Turkey-based allied air force, known as Operation Provide Comfort, is due to go before the Turkish parliament by the end of this year.

Turkey and the allies are negotiating minor alterations to the force, including a name change. The operation lost some effectiveness in Kurdish infighting in northern Iraq four months ago when one Kurdish faction got backing from Iraqi troops.

Washington had to scrap Provide Comfort's ground operations in northern Iraq and evacuated staff there but the air patrol operation has continued. Provide Comfort was set up after a failed Iraqi Kurdish uprising in 1991 following the Gulf War.

Turkish MPs often complain the air shield has helped create a power vacuum exploited by Turkish Kurd rebels in northern Iraq. The Turkish Kurdish rebels use the area as a staging ground for attacks on southeast Turkey, where they want to set up an independent or federative Kurdish state.
